target_window: 2024Q4 through 2026Q2; classification describes the policy-period institutional rules, not a historical state panel
basis: Statutory/agency coverage of H-2A service, not benefit eligibility or observed employment discrepancies. Voluntary coverage, employer thresholds, localized employment and errors in industry reporting prevent a categorical domestic-only interpretation.
default: ambiguous: national FUTA exemptions do not establish a state's UI reporting law

06.basis: Interpretation of EDD's express coverage of direct and registered-contractor agricultural labor, and its nonresident exclusions limited to other specified visa/service categories; subject to employer eligibility and localization.

12.basis: Florida 443.1216(13)(x) excludes qualifying H-2A agricultural service; agency explicitly says exempt workers should not be reported. Services outside agricultural labor need separate classification.

27.basis: 268.035 subd.20(36) excludes employment under the H-2A agricultural program, regardless of direct/contractor employer; voluntary coverage is possible.

36.basis: Agency guidance effective 2020 excludes H-2A services/remuneration and separately explains crew-leader liability; voluntary coverage remains possible.

41.basis: 2025 legislative staff summary says H-2A employers pay UI but proposed exemption's final effective status for the full window is unresolved; no assumption from proposal.

48.basis: Agency statute search excerpt indicates H-2A exemption but full PDF returned a browser challenge; unresolved in this frozen classification.

53.basis: Interpretation of broad agricultural employment under RCW50.04.150 and explicit direct/crew-leader treatment in .155; no H-2A exclusion in these provisions. Tax coverage, not eligibility to collect benefits.
